intro: You are about to enter Mahmut Bey Mosque, a mosque and complex in Kastamonu province, dating from 1366. Here is its secret: it was built entirely by interlocking joinery, without a single nail. And look up — its ceiling and capitals still carry their six-hundred-and-fifty-year-old original paintwork.
history: This mosque in the village of Kasaba near Kastamonu was built in 1366 for Mahmut Bey of the Candarid dynasty. Its posts, beams and ceiling are all joined by interlocking joinery, without a single nail. The painted decoration on the ceiling and capitals is original; in six hundred and fifty years it has never been renewed. In 2023 it entered the World Heritage List.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the nail-free timber frame and the original painted ceiling, then the walnut door leaves and the carved capitals.
facts: Did you know? The mosque's walnut doors were displayed for years in the Ethnography Museum in Ankara; only copies went back to the building. Its timber frame and ceiling are joined entirely by interlocking joinery, without a single nail. And the painted decoration on the ceiling and capitals is still the original after six hundred and fifty years — it has never been renewed.
outro: This brings our tour of Mahmut Bey Mosque to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for your visit, and enjoy the rest of your day.
